title: edgecase-rollforward-requests-lanecard-2026-09-08
summary: Compact synthesis of small but high-friction runtime asks from customers around rollforward behavior, streaming cutovers, model-variant fallbacks, and telemetry blindspots. Purpose: create a lanecard of low-effort patches, prioritized hypotheses, and experimental guardrails we can trial in the next sprint without large infra churn.
vignettes: SaaS-A: long-running chat sessions (~30m) experienced token duplication when a regional failover retried the last chunk; customer patched client-side but asks server-side de-dup and clearer retry headers.

Marketplace-B: uses dedicated pools + burst; on canary -> main rollout some requests switched quantized model variant mid-KV-cache leading to hallucinated completions. They want automatic KV-cache invalidation or compatibility labeling.
FinReg-C: private deployment showed silent truncation when downstream function-calling returned an empty JSON; they want explicit status codes and a small diagnostic blob in audit logs.

EdgeApp-D: intermittent 503s during short spikes; client retried aggressively causing ordering issues in streaming clients. They want backoff hints and a server-side monotonic sequence id per stream to detect reorder.

StartUp-E: observed a latency cliff when sequence-length distribution changed (client upgraded prompt templates). They ask for a per-customer sequence-length histogram alert + suggested kernel/quantization profile.

MLPlatform-F: multiple tenants request opt-in graceful degradation: when preferred model unavailable, route to cheaper variant but mark response with provenance + uncertainty score for app-level gating.
consolidated-asks: 1) streaming-retry-safety: add sequence-id per stream + idempotent-retry behavior documented and surfaced in responses
2) kv-cache-compatibility-metadata: label model variants with cache-compatibility flags and add API to invalidate cache keys across variant families
3) audit-diagnostic-blob: small base64-encoded diagnostic field on failure paths (opt-in) for private deployments
4) fallback-provenance: when routing to a fallback model, include variant provenance and an uncertainty hint in response headers
5) per-tenant seq-len telemetry: lightweight histogram and alerting threshold in Console
6) backoff-hints: expose recommended retry backoff in 5xx/429 responses for streaming and chunked endpoints
proposals: A. Quickpatch (1 sprint): attach monotonic stream-sequence-id and accept client-provided idempotency-token. Minimal router+ingress changes; add unit tests and a short section in SDKs.
B. Mid (2-3 sprints): add model-variant cache-compatibility labeling. Requires model catalog schema change and a KV-cache invalidation API. Start with a whitelist approach for verified variants.
C. Audit opt-in (1 sprint + config): add small diagnostic blob stored in audit logs and echoed in response for private deployments; gated by per-customer setting to avoid storage growth.
D. Fallback provenance (1 sprint): include fallback metadata in response headers (model-id, reason-code, uncertainty-score). Stopgap: header only; long-term: structured response field.
E. Telemetry alpha (1 sprint): emit per-tenant seq-len histogram metric to our metrics backend with retention 7d and Console chart tile; evaluate later for Alerting integration.
F. Backoff hint (quick): standardize Retry-After-like header for chunked/streaming endpoints; include suggested jitter ranges in SDK docs.
impact_estimates: A (stream-seq-id): customer pain high (reorders/dup), infra effort low; expected reduction in CS tickets ~40% for streaming issues
B (kv-compat): customer pain medium-high, infra effort medium; reduces hallucination incidents after variant rollouts, prevents subtle correctness regressions
C (audit-blob): customer pain medium, infra effort low; high value for compliance customers and triage speed
D (fallback-provenance): customer pain medium, effort low; increases trust when automatic fallbacks occur
E (telemetry): customer pain medium, effort low; helps preempt cost/latency surprises caused by prompt changes
F (backoff): customer pain high for retry storms, effort very low; quick wins to reduce cascade failures
open_questions: What is the minimum payload for the diagnostic blob that satisfies FinReg-C without exposing PII?
Do we require a model-variant semantic version to compute cache-compatibility or is a hash-based fingerprint sufficient?
How do we prevent telemetry emission from costing customers extra? opt-in vs opt-out?
Should fallback uncertainty be a normalized 0-1 score or coarse buckets (low/med/high) to simplify client logic?
Is stream-seq-id enforceable for all ingress types (HTTP/GRPC/Websocket) without breaking existing SDKs?
quick_patches: 1) Add Retry-Hint header with 'min-ms' and 'max-ms' for streaming endpoints (docs + ingress change)
2) Return 'X-Rollforward-Provenance' header when a request switches variants mid-request (header-only flag, no structured body)
3) Console: add temporary 'recent-seq-len-sample' tile per-tenant (UI + small metric emitter)
implementation-risks: Race conditions when adding seq-id to existing streaming flows — need careful contract tests with SDK teams
Cache-invalidation for variant families could cause cold-start regressions if misused; require gradual opt-in and experimentation
Diagnostic blob can be abused for large payloads; enforce strict size and scrub rules
Headers-only provenance is easy but may be missed by users that rely on structured responses
rollout_plan: Phase 0: ship quick patches (Retry-Hint header, provenance header, Console seq-len tile) behind feature flags and soft-launch to 20% of traffic. Phase 1: enable stream-seq-id and idempotency-token for new SDK versions; monitor error/dup metrics for 2 weeks. Phase 2: deploy model-variant labeling to model catalog and expose KV-invalidate API to a pilot group. Phase 3: audit-blob opt-in for Private customers and iterate on size/schema.

Open a small spike PR for Retry-Hint header and update SDKs (owner: Sofia)
Design doc for model-variant compatibility schema (owner: Tom Becker) - target review by 2026-09-20

Create dashboard card for 'stream dedup/duplicate-rate' and add to oncall runbook
notes_to_self: Keep patches as header-first to minimize structured API churn. Emphasize opt-ins for telemetry/audit data to avoid billing/customer-data concerns. Coordinate with legal for audit blob schema if FinReg customers involved.
